# Get-ZbxSli

## SYNOPSIS

Gets the service level indicators of an SLA.

## SYNTAX

```
Get-ZbxSli [-Sla] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixSlaRecord>> [-PeriodFrom <DateTimeOffset>] [-PeriodTo <DateTimeOffset>] [-Periods <int>] [-ServiceId <ulong[]>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Get-ZbxSli cmdlet reads an SLA's report with sla.getsli: for each reporting period and each service the SLA covers, the uptime, downtime, error budget and the SLI reached. By default it reports the SLA's recent periods; -PeriodFrom, -PeriodTo and -Periods choose others, and -ServiceId narrows the services. It writes one object as the server sent it and needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Get an SLA's report

```powershell
Get-ZbxSli -Sla 'Business hours SLA'
```

-Sla (position 0) takes the SLA's name, id or object.

### Example 2: Get the last four weeks of an SLA piped from Get-ZbxSla

```powershell
Get-ZbxSla -Name 'Business hours SLA' | Get-ZbxSli -Periods 4
```

-Periods sets how many reporting periods (here weeks) the report covers.
